title: The Commons Public Hours ☕
description:
🎉 Public Hours at the Commons 🎉

Every Sunday, the Commons opens to the public — no membership required. Come co-work, connect, create, or just explore the space at your own pace. ✨

🕘 When: Every Sunday, 9 AM – 10 PM

📍 Where: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco (corner of Hayes & Laguna, basement level)

RSVP and we'll email you your entry code ahead of time — so you can let yourself straight in when you arrive.

──────────────────────────────

🧭 A self-guided day

Public Hours are self-guided — come in, settle in, and make the space your own. Weekends are usually unstaffed, so there's no check-in desk or guided tour. Our members are glad to answer questions about the space; for anything else — including guided tours, which we don't offer as drop-ins — email hello@thesfcommons.com ahead of time.

──────────────────────────────

🔭 Getting in

Your entry code comes by email. Once you RSVP, we'll send you a personal QR code — that's your key for the day. Keep it handy on your phone (and check spam if you don't see it).

• Find us. We're at 540 Laguna St, on the corner of Hayes & Laguna. Head down the stairs beside Earthbody to the basement level — that's the Commons.
• Scan your QR code at the reader to unlock the door. Hold your phone just below the Kisi reader by the door and it'll let you in.

Your access stays active all day, 9 AM – 10 PM, so you can come and go freely.

Can't find your code on the day? No problem — scan the QR posted on the door to check in and get a fresh one on the spot.

We're shoes-off 🧦 — please clean up after yourself, including dirty dishes and mugs, and use only the front entrance. Trouble getting in? Email hello@thesfcommons.com.

The Commons is a modern-day town square for communal meaning-making, personal discovery, and self-expression in the heart of San Francisco. Apply to become a member here__.

title: What Should Stay Human?
description:
AI is changing how we work and live, fast. Some of us are excited, some are worried, most of us are both. In the middle of it all, what makes us human—and what kind of future do we want to create?

This is a space to slow down, reconnect with ourselves and each other, and make sense of this change together. Through simple body-based practices, shared stories, and honest conversation, we’ll explore what has carried us through change before and what can guide us now.

Who it’s for

Anyone feeling the change: founders, business owners, people navigating shifts at work, and builders and scientists shaping AI. No tech background needed. Worried or excited, you belong here.

What we’ll explore together

• What makes us feel alive, connected, and human
• What’s changing in our work and lives, and how it’s affecting us
• What the future of work could look like—and what we want to help shape
• What we choose to keep human, and how we can navigate what comes next together

We’ll bring our bodies, feelings, and imagination into the exploration alongside our ideas. Everyone helps shape the conversation.

What you’ll leave with

More clarity about what matters to you. One intentional choice about how you want to move forward. And the experience of meeting this change with others.

In person. Small group. Bring your whole self.

Facilitated by Nima Imani & Annalisa Jackson

Nima is a founder and ICF-certified leadership coach helping founders, leaders, and teams navigate uncertainty, hard decisions, and the human side of change.

Annalisa is an ICF-certified somatic coach and facilitator who uses mindfulness and body-based practices to help people find their ground in uncertainty, trust their choices, and communicate with clarity and confidence under pressure.

About InsightsOut

InsightsOut works with individuals and organizations on the human side of AI change and leadership.

title: Community & Belonging Circles
description:
🌿 Description

A weekly space for real conversations, meaningful connection, and a deeper sense of belonging.

🌿 About This Gathering

Maybe you've got plenty of people in your life, but still sometimes feel lonely. Maybe you find it hard to move beyond small talk and social scripts. Maybe you sometimes struggle to feel like you truly belong, even when you're surrounded by people. Or maybe you're simply curious about what makes some relationships and communities feel easy, genuine, and nourishing — while others don't.

Each week, we'll explore a different aspect of connection and belonging: loneliness, vulnerability, authenticity, being seen, boundaries, desire, conflict, and what gets in the way of feeling connected and at home with others.

This isn't a workshop where you sit and listen to someone talk about connection. We'll actually practice connecting with one another. You'll have opportunities to share honestly, meet others more deeply, receive support, and explore what's happening in your own relationships and your experience of belonging.

You don't need to have a particular problem or goal. Just bring yourself, some curiosity, and a willingness to connect.

💫 Who This Is For

For anyone who wants more genuine connection and a deeper sense of belonging. Especially if you sometimes struggle to connect, fit in, or feel truly at home with others — or if you're simply looking for relationships that go beyond small talk and social scripts

🎒 Facilitator

Simone Giacometti is a somatic practitioner, psychedelic integration guide, and facilitator passionate about helping people connect more deeply with themselves and others

🏛 About The Commons

🚪The Commons is a community-based "Fourth Place" that catalyzes each member's path to authenticity, full self-expression, and aliveness - rooted in the belief that community is essential to that journey. title: Command Line Music - Auwen Workshop
description:
This class is an intro to command line music with Auwen, a tool for writing and performing songs in real time using a command line interface.

You'll get hands-on experience building tracks from scratch and playing them in a low stakes, collaborative setting. No prior coding or music experience needed.

What to expect: installation takes about 5 minutes. Your first beat, maybe an hour. Playing a full set takes a 3-6 weeks of practice depending on experience level.

A few students have gone on to perform live sets at SF events and festivals as part of Soniare Collective. With just a bit of dedication you could be next! We would love to have you join our growing family of music producers.

After the class you'll be invited to our Discord where we do multiplayer jam sessions, so there's space to keep learning and playing with other people.

Workshop Outline

• Software and sample installation
• Overview of Auwen User Interface and workflow
• Multiplayer learning session creating genres you suggest
• Solo time creating music on your own computer
• Wrap-up and share resources for further learning

Educational Goals

To inspire participants and offer an accessible entry point into performing live dance music, while building foundational skills in livecoding, composition, improvisation, and real-time musical decision-making.

Instructor

Nes Croft is a musician, artist, and computer engineer from Montana who has written and recorded thousands of songs since a young age starting with folk/rock as a teenager and expanding into experimental pop, IDM, techno, and trance. Nes gained an interest in electronics at age 19 after working at the DIY synth company Synthrotek in Portland, OR. Going on to earn a bachelor's degree in computer engineering at Montana State University. While in college Nes co-founded and developed Vaytricks Beat Machine, a mobile drum machine app that received over 100,000 downloads. 5 years later Nes left Vaytricks to pursue a live performance focused approach to music production and Auwen was born. Auwen is a digital audio workstation featuring a hybrid producer/DJ workflow that allows musicians to perform dance music live using a command line interface. Given the nature of the software, Nes naturally gravitated toward live music events testing Auwen at various electronic music festivals in Montana. Later, Nes joined the livecoding scene in San Francisco and started hosting workshops & live music events at TIAT art gallery and Gray Area in San Francisco in 2025-2026.

Preparation

Bring a laptop/headphones and install the software auwen.app to save time in class. Also bring water and maybe a light snack to keep your energy up because we'll be covering a lot of information! Some drinks may be provided as well. When you arrive come through the front of TIAT then all the way back and down the stairs on the left. The event is in the TIAT basement.

Beyond small talk, social scripts, and the pressure to be a certain way.

Through movement, playfulness, meaningful conversation, inner exploration, and consensual touch, we’ll explore what helps us feel more at ease, show up more authentically, and connect more deeply with others - all within a trauma-informed space.

🌿 About This Gathering

Meaningful connection rarely happens by accident. It tends to emerge when we feel safe enough to slow down, be ourselves, and meet one another with curiosity.

This gathering is an invitation to explore what makes genuine connection possible — not by performing, saying the “right” thing, or following a script, but by creating the conditions for greater presence, playfulness, and authenticity with ourselves and others.

At the heart of this gathering is a simple idea: connection deepens when we feel safe enough to be seen and express ourselves — not just the polished parts, but also the parts we might usually hide or hold back. Through movement, play, somatic awareness, shadow work, and guided conversations, we'll explore what happens when we allow ourselves to be more visible and meet one another with greater openness.

Through these experiences, we'll practice meeting moments of vulnerability with choice and support. We'll explore what becomes possible when we let ourselves be seen more fully while staying connected to others — without having to sacrifice our sense of belonging.

This is an evolving exploration of connection, community, and play. I'm excited to create this experience together and discover what unfolds when we give ourselves more room for authenticity, curiosity, and genuine connection.

🕰 Flow / Schedule

11:00 – 11:15: Arrival & settling in

11:15 – 11:30: Welcome & agreements

11:30 – 2:30: Exploring connection — one-to-one & small groups

2:30 – 3:15: Lunch Break

3:15 – 5:00: Exploring connections: the inner game of connection

5:00 – 5:15: Break

5:15 – 6:45: Exploring connection — group dynamics

6:45 – 7:00: Closing circle

7:00 onward: Stay, mingle & continue connecting (if you want to)

💫 Who This Is For

This gathering is for anyone who longs for more genuine connection. It’s especially for people who sometimes struggle to connect, fit in, or feel like they truly belong; for those who appreciate a slower pace when getting to know others; and for anyone curious about moving beyond small talk, social performance, or the feeling that they need to say the “right” thing or show up in a certain way.

Rather than trying to “get connection right,” we’ll explore what naturally allows connection to emerge—through presence, play, movement, and authentic conversation.

Whether you're outgoing, introverted, or somewhere in between, you'll be invited to participate at your own pace. No previous experience is needed: just come as you are.

👥 Facilitator

Simone Giacometti is a somatic practitioner, psychedelic integration guide, and facilitator passionate about helping people heal, grow, and connect more deeply with themselves and others.

Originally trained as a scientist, Simone spent years working at the intersection of biology, technology, and program management before transitioning into healing work. Today, he supports people through one-on-one sessions that weave together trauma-informed healing, somatic practices, inner exploration, and psychedelic integration work to help people reconnect with themselves and grow into greater authenticity.

His group facilitation draws on somatics, authentic relating, nervous system awareness, and play to create spaces where people can slow down, be themselves, and feel more at home with others. (This gathering is fully substance-free and centered on movement, conversation, and connection.)

Learn more about Simone and his work at healwithsimone.com

🎒 What to Bring

Lunch

Comfortable clothes you can move in

A water bottle (optional)

Curiosity and a willingness to meet yourself and others as you are.

🏛 About The Commons

The Commons is a community-based "Fourth Place" that catalyzes each member's path to authenticity, full self-expression, and aliveness - rooted in the belief that community is essential to that journey. Located in the heart of San Francisco, we are redefining what it means to gather, work, and connect. By day, we're a playful co-working space; by night, a vibrant community meeting house.

title: Perverting the Everyday: Co-speculating a Strange Product Catalogue
description:
*Designing faux product pages for the strange appliances of an alternate reality.

Perversion of Interfaces is a collection of objects that claim to be “smart,” but often fail, misbehave, or do something anomalous. A camera that resists taking pictures, a smart light that longs for intimacy, or a prescription device that does face-reading. They are familiar, humorous, worrisome at times, and mostly confusing.

This workshop builds on this notion of "perverting," inviting participants to imagine an alternate reality where "smart" products diverge from contemporary design norms. Drawing from the exhibition's theme of wildly expressive computers, participants will take a familiar, mundane home appliance and completely reimagine its lifecycle.

This will be a participatory, conversational workshop where we will work in small teams to make pitches for speculative products, imagine product-consumer lifecycles, and produce an online catalogue as an archive for our collective "perversion" of familiar objects and rituals.

The workshop will take about 2.5 hours and we recommend bringing laptops!

Agenda

• 20 min - Intro and Conversation
• 20 min - Product Pitch
• 1 hour - Concept Development in Groups
• 20 min - "All Hands Review"
• 30 min - Finalization and Launch Celebration

About your instructor

Sang is an Assistant Professor in the Human-Centered Design program at Cornell University, where his research focuses on the notion of symbiosis between human and technology through making. His current interest lies in new horizons of AI systems that are interpretive, embodied, and entangled. Through the design of alternative technology artifacts, he envisions new forms of human-computer relationship that better support individualities, somatic experiences, and long-term engagement. He leads the Machine Poetics Lab, which engages in a mix of art, engineering, and empirical methods to explore future technology experiences.

description:
Gather with neighbors at the Autumn Neighborhood Ingathering, where we will come together to honor our encounters with loss and the turn of the season.

In our lives, we all experience loss of all sizes (great and small – people, hopes, chapters of life, etc.) that deserve the space to be honored and held. Sample schedule:

• Intro to the turn of the season

• Altar creation ceremony (representing a loss in clay)
• Breakout activities (choose your own adventure)
• Altar release ceremony (salt and re-membering)

What to bring:

• Optional: If you want to bring a memento (e.g. a photo or keepsake) of something or someone you have lost as a supplement to the altar creation ceremony, you may do so. Decorations like flowers are also welcome!

description:
What if your water bottle had opinions? What if your sketchbook could critique your art?

Audio Lab is a hands-on experiment in giving everyday things a voice. After a short talk on how technology is reshaping our relationships with the objects around us, you’ll wander through several installations, some familiar, some unexpected, each with its own voice and personality.

We’ll learn how objects have been personified in media, popular culture, and the tech of the past and present. Attendees will interact with each installation and ponder what would happen if the encouraging one turned sarcastic? What if it sounded like your uncle? Remix the personas, test your reactions, and help imagine what this new era of talking things could, or should, feel like.

This workshop is for the curious minds who are willing to talk to things that usually stay quiet.

Who This Is For

People working on software, hardware, businesses, creative projects, writing, design, research, art, anything you're trying to make real. Come if you want accountability, momentum, and the energy of working alongside others. First-timers and regulars both welcome.

What to Bring

Laptop, notebook, sketchbook, instrument, whatever tools your project requires. Come with something to work on, or come ready to figure out what that is.

Norms

Respect the deep work sprint by keeping conversation low during focused time. Share-back is how we learn from each other: share what you built, ask for what you need, and offer what you can. Everyone participates.

🌿 Description

An experiential workshop blending nervous system science with meditation, somatic practice, and relational exercises.

🌿 About This Gathering

Most of us have spent a lot of our lives collecting knowledge, figuring things out, and trying to stay in control. In the age of AI, information is more abundant than ever. What we need now may be the capacity to step out of cognitive loops, meet uncertainty, listen to our innate intelligence, and embody forms of wisdom beyond the analytical mind.

The Unknowing Lab is an exploration of science, spirituality, and the art of not knowing.

Across contemplative traditions, we find teachings that invite us to relax the conceptual mind and experience reality more directly. Neuroscience, psychology, and nervous system research are now giving us new ways to understand why these practices can be transformative—and why letting go of familiar identities, predictions, and patterns can also feel vulnerable.

We’ll explore some of that science, but we won’t stop at analyzing it. We’ll become our own researchers, using meditation, somatic practice, play, and relational inquiry to discover what unknowing actually feels like in the body.
This is a space to move from insight to embodiment: to let the nervous system rest, loosen habitual patterns, open to creativity and possibility, and meet life with a little less friction and a little more curiosity, trust, and participation.

🕰 Flow

Arrival + Intention

Connecting with what brings us here and what we hope to explore.

Science + Spiritual Wisdom

A grounded introduction to unknowing and the relationship between awareness, nervous system regulation, and loosening the conceptual self.

Embodied Practices

Gentle regulation, resourcing, meditation, and playful experiments that invite curiosity and new ways of perceiving.

Relational Inquiry

Partner practices where we experiment with staying present, connected, and open while investigating our relationship to unknowing.

Integration + Closing

Reflecting on what we discovered and how it might live beyond the workshop.

👥 Facilitator

Pauline Romas is a somatic facilitator, community builder, and lifelong student of the divine mystery. She brings her background as an engineer and thousands of hours of meditation practice to her work with embodiment and the nervous system. Pauline creates spaces of unconditional acceptance where people can connect with their heart’s wisdom and inner guidance to explore new ways of living and relating, bringing their spiritual insights into everyday life.

Learn more about Pauline and her work at PaulineRomas.love

This gathering is for curious humans who spend a lot of time in their heads, feel drawn to the intersection of science and spirituality, or long to embody what they already know intellectually.

Our bodies hold onto the activation and reactive patterns that keep us stuck, but they also hold the key to being able to feel and respond differently.

Somatic practice gives us a way to rewire how we relate in love and connection, not just understand it.

This is a monthly practice lab where you'll reflect on who you want to be in romantic connection, and learn embodied practices that help you:

Command Line Music - Auwen Workshop
description:
This class is an intro to command line music with Auwen, a tool for writing and performing songs in real time using a command line interface.

You'll get hands-on experience building tracks from scratch and playing them in a low stakes, collaborative setting. No prior coding or music experience needed.

What to expect: installation takes about 5 minutes. Your first beat, maybe an hour. Playing a full set takes a 3-6 weeks of practice depending on experience level.

A few students have gone on to perform live sets at SF events and festivals as part of Soniare Collective. With just a bit of dedication you could be next! We would love to have you join our growing family of music producers.

After the class you'll be invited to our Discord where we do multiplayer jam sessions, so there's space to keep learning and playing with other people.

Workshop Outline

• Software and sample installation
• Overview of Auwen User Interface and workflow
• Multiplayer learning session creating genres you suggest
• Solo time creating music on your own computer
• Wrap-up and share resources for further learning

Educational Goals

To inspire participants and offer an accessible entry point into performing live dance music, while building foundational skills in livecoding, composition, improvisation, and real-time musical decision-making.

Instructor

Nes Croft is a musician, artist, and computer engineer from Montana who has written and recorded thousands of songs since a young age starting with folk/rock as a teenager and expanding into experimental pop, IDM, techno, and trance. Nes gained an interest in electronics at age 19 after working at the DIY synth company Synthrotek in Portland, OR. Going on to earn a bachelor's degree in computer engineering at Montana State University. While in college Nes co-founded and developed Vaytricks Beat Machine, a mobile drum machine app that received over 100,000 downloads. 5 years later Nes left Vaytricks to pursue a live performance focused approach to music production and Auwen was born. Auwen is a digital audio workstation featuring a hybrid producer/DJ workflow that allows musicians to perform dance music live using a command line interface. Given the nature of the software, Nes naturally gravitated toward live music events testing Auwen at various electronic music festivals in Montana. Later, Nes joined the livecoding scene in San Francisco and started hosting workshops & live music events at TIAT art gallery and Gray Area in San Francisco in 2025-2026.

Preparation

Bring a laptop/headphones and install the software auwen.app to save time in class. Also bring water and maybe a light snack to keep your energy up because we'll be covering a lot of information! Some drinks may be provided as well. When you arrive come through the front of TIAT then all the way back and down the stairs on the left. The event is in the TIAT basement.

Every Sunday, the Commons opens to the public — no membership required. Come co-work, connect, create, or just explore the space at your own pace. ✨

RSVP and we'll email you your entry code ahead of time — so you can let yourself straight in when you arrive.

🧭 A self-guided day

Public Hours are self-guided — come in, settle in, and make the space your own. Weekends are usually unstaffed, so there's no check-in desk or guided tour. Our members are glad to answer questions about the space; for anything else — including guided tours, which we don't offer as drop-ins — email hello@thesfcommons.com ahead of time.

🔭 Getting in

Your entry code comes by email. Once you RSVP, we'll send you a personal QR code — that's your key for the day. Keep it handy on your phone (and check spam if you don't see it).

• Find us. We're at 540 Laguna St, on the corner of Hayes & Laguna. Head down the stairs beside Earthbody to the basement level — that's the Commons.
• Scan your QR code at the reader to unlock the door. Hold your phone just below the Kisi reader by the door and it'll let you in.

Your access stays active all day, 9 AM – 10 PM, so you can come and go freely.

Can't find your code on the day? No problem — scan the QR posted on the door to check in and get a fresh one on the spot.

We're shoes-off 🧦 — please clean up after yourself, including dirty dishes and mugs, and use only the front entrance. Trouble getting in? Email hello@thesfcommons.com.

title: Command Line Music - Auwen Workshop
description:
This class is an intro to command line music with Auwen, a tool for writing and performing songs in real time using a command line interface.

You'll get hands-on experience building tracks from scratch and playing them in a low stakes, collaborative setting. No prior coding or music experience needed.

What to expect: installation takes about 5 minutes. Your first beat, maybe an hour. Playing a full set takes a 3-6 weeks of practice depending on experience level.

A few students have gone on to perform live sets at SF events and festivals as part of Soniare Collective. With just a bit of dedication you could be next! We would love to have you join our growing family of music producers.

After the class you'll be invited to our Discord where we do multiplayer jam sessions, so there's space to keep learning and playing with other people.

Workshop Outline

• Software and sample installation
• Overview of Auwen User Interface and workflow
• Multiplayer learning session creating genres you suggest
• Solo time creating music on your own computer
• Wrap-up and share resources for further learning

Educational Goals

To inspire participants and offer an accessible entry point into performing live dance music, while building foundational skills in livecoding, composition, improvisation, and real-time musical decision-making.

Instructor

Nes Croft is a musician, artist, and computer engineer from Montana who has written and recorded thousands of songs since a young age starting with folk/rock as a teenager and expanding into experimental pop, IDM, techno, and trance. Nes gained an interest in electronics at age 19 after working at the DIY synth company Synthrotek in Portland, OR. Going on to earn a bachelor's degree in computer engineering at Montana State University. While in college Nes co-founded and developed Vaytricks Beat Machine, a mobile drum machine app that received over 100,000 downloads. 5 years later Nes left Vaytricks to pursue a live performance focused approach to music production and Auwen was born. Auwen is a digital audio workstation featuring a hybrid producer/DJ workflow that allows musicians to perform dance music live using a command line interface. Given the nature of the software, Nes naturally gravitated toward live music events testing Auwen at various electronic music festivals in Montana. Later, Nes joined the livecoding scene in San Francisco and started hosting workshops & live music events at TIAT art gallery and Gray Area in San Francisco in 2025-2026.

Preparation

Bring a laptop/headphones and install the software auwen.app to save time in class. Also bring water and maybe a light snack to keep your energy up because we'll be covering a lot of information! Some drinks may be provided as well. When you arrive come through the front of TIAT then all the way back and down the stairs on the left. The event is in the TIAT basement.

Write & Mingle: 6pm to 7pm
Share on Stage: 7pm to 8pm
Drink & Discuss: 8pm to 9pm
